progress_log.summary: goal_control:pause — User interrupted with a blocking cross-clip adjust bleed bug; pausing colour roadmap to fix it first.

evidence.description: Fixed the cross-clip adjust bleed. Root cause: `TimelineManager.previewOverlay` was a scene-wide `Map<elementId, patch>` and `commitPreview()` promoted EVERY staged entry in one TracksSnapshotCommand, so a gesture staged on clip 1 and interrupted (panel unmounted mid-drag) was promoted inside clip 2's commit. Fixes: (1) overlay keyed by `trackId:elementId` (collisions across tracks impossible), (2) new `commitPreviewForElement`/`discardPreviewForElement` promote only the caller's own entry, (3) `resolveStalePreviews()` wired to selection changes in `EditorCore` so a stranded entry is resolved BEFORE the new clip can stage/commit, (4) `useElementPreview` tracks its own staged write and commits it on unmount/target change, (5) all single-element commit sites scoped (image/audio/blending/masks/graphic tabs, 3 keyframed property hooks, transform/mask canvas handles, text-edit commit) — scene-wide commit kept only for the genuine multi-element group drag in use-preview-interaction, (6) `commitPreview` now recomputes from current committed tracks instead of promoting the possibly-stale `previewTracks` snapshot, (7) `Apply all` in adjust-tab was a no-op (main track only, patch undefined) and now writes the real adjustment values to every selected target in one undo step. New regression suite `preview-overlay-bleed.test.ts` (6 tests) covers clip-2 commit not promoting clip 1, stale resolution on selection change, same-id-different-track isolation, and committed-write supersession.

Full unit suite + typecheck + lint after the cross-clip bleed fix. `bun test --isolate src/` in apps/web: 1256 pass, 11 skip (Redis-only), 0 fail across 206 files. `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `biome check` on all 16 touched files: no fixes needed. New tests: 6/6 pass.

evidence.description: Renderer unit suite for the ImageBitmap ownership fix. Ran `bun test --isolate apps/web/src/services/renderer` before and after: the two new regression tests ("keeps a cached source usable after the shared decode LRU overflows" for image and sticker caches) FAILED before the fix (expected bitmap.closed=false, got true) and PASS after adding detachDecodedBitmap ownership transfer. Full suite 189 pass / 0 fail across 24 files. Proves a bitmap the render path was still serving was being closed by a second cache owner, and a closed ImageBitmap uploads as nothing (a black layer).

Black-preview root cause isolated by controlled browser measurement (headed Chromium, real WebGPU adapter, disposable project). With ZERO elements on the timeline the console recorded createBuffer size failures: 1, followed by 'RefCell already borrowed' at rust/wasm/src/compositor.rs:167: 542. Proves the preview is not black because of the photo (the timeline thumbnail renders the same photo correctly); the compositor bricks itself on the first degenerate texture dimension and every later frame panics. Also established that headless SwiftShader reports navigator.gpu.requestAdapter() === null, so headless runs give a false 'black preview' verdict and cannot be used as evidence for this class of bug.

Uniform-pool mid-frame recycle aliasing fixed and proven. Root cause: pipeline.rs called UniformBufferPool::recycle_frame() per pass and masks per application, while the whole frame records into ONE encoder submitted once at frame end — LIFO pop handed pass N+1 the same buffer as pass N, so the later Queue::write_buffer (staged before submit) clobbered the earlier draw's uniforms. Browser mechanism probe (headed Chromium WebGPU, readback via copyTextureToBuffer, no present): distinct-buffer case pass1=(255,0,0,255) red / pass2=(0,0,255,255) blue; shared-buffer case pass1=(0,0,255,255) BLUE despite red written first — mechanism confirmed in this browser. Fix: recycle_frame moved to the frame boundary (compositor render_frame/render_frame_to_bytes call effects.recycle_frame() + masks.recycle_frame(); standalone apply()/apply_mask_feather() recycle themselves once per own-encoder submit). Regression test chains_within_one_frame_never_share_buffers added to uniform_pool.rs; cargo test -p gpu -p compositor -p effects -p masks = 26 pass (gpu 5, compositor 9, effects 12), wasm rebuilt (14:48). App verification with fresh dev server: store holds 3 simultaneous effect passes (exposure -100, tint-shift +100, sharpen +50), 0 console errors, 0 createBuffer failures across a 6s settle. Same probe also proves SwiftShader rasterization works (clear-only readback red) while present-to-canvas reads [0,0,0,0] — the black DOM preview in the test environment is a present limitation, not a render-path defect.

t-9 GPU/Rust performance track completed with 10 documented rounds in docs/features/editor-perf-100-pass/gpu.md. Headline benchmark (deterministic, cargo test -p gpu steady_state_frames_allocate_no_buffers): a 3-layer frame with a 2-pass effect chain and a feathered mask = 19 uniform-buffer acquires per frame; before the pool every acquire was a create_buffer_init mapped allocation (19/frame forever = 950 across 50 frames); after the pool 950 acquires produce 19 total allocations and every subsequent frame records ZERO — 98% allocation reduction plus complete elimination of the mappedAtCreation path that caused the panic class. Supporting evidence: grep shows 0 mapped_at_creation:true and 6 acquire_uniform call sites (only remaining create_buffer_init is the one-time fullscreen quad at context init); full Rust suite 27 pass / 0 fail (gpu 6, compositor 9, effects 12); wasm rebuilt 3,111,775 bytes verified newer than all sources; browser run with 3 simultaneous effect passes = 0 console errors, 0 createBuffer failures. Full web suite after fixes: bun test --isolate src/ = 1111 pass / 0 fail / 11 skip; bunx tsc --noEmit clean; biome clean on all touched files. Two stale tests fixed en route: canvas-renderer.clamp.test.ts integration expectation contradicted the file's own unit contract (non-finite contains to MIN) — now uses finite runaway 1e12; registry-render-boundary.test.ts IMAGE tab list was missing the new 'adjust' tab.

t-2/t-3/t-4 verified in one headed Playwright run on the fresh dev server. t-2 Transitions+Motion with real photos: two fixture photos dropped onto two different tracks (full time overlap), both clips multi-selected, Transitions tab card click produced toast "Fade added / Transition inserted between the two clips.", Motion tab card click produced "Fade Up applied", then Space-playback through the transition region for 4s recorded ZERO console errors and ZERO createBuffer failures — transitions and motion render paths are regression-clean. t-3 Sound 401: root cause was the auth-gated /api/sounds/search being fired while signed out (console 401 + silent empty tab). Fix: SoundsView and useSoundSearch now resolve the better-auth session first (useSession) and skip the doomed request entirely when signed out, rendering an explicit localized "Sign in to browse the sound library" state (en+id dictionary keys added). Verified twice: zero /api/sounds network requests fired while signed out, session endpoint returns 200/null, and the auth message renders in the Audio tab (the sounds view is reachable via the Audio tab — "sounds" is not in VISIBLE_TAB_KEYS). t-4 Arth AI panel: no positional defect reproduces — measured geometry: AI view at (89,49,415x539) fully inside the 1600x950 viewport, clear of the tab rail (x 89 >= rail right edge 80), composer textarea at bottom of the chat column (y 504/539-height view, 84% down); typing in the composer produced no errors. tsc --noEmit clean, biome check clean on sounds.tsx, use-sound-search.ts, dictionaries.ts.

Black preview on real-GPU browsers root-caused and fixed. Reproduced on the user's actual configuration (headed Chromium, NO test GPU flags, NVIDIA lovelace adapter, bgra8unorm preferred): photo dropped on timeline + Space playback → preview canvas fully black (4096/4096 sampled pixels black) with repeating WebGPU validation errors "[Texture compositor-layer] usage (TextureBinding|RenderAttachment) includes writable usage and another usage in the same synchronization scope" and every frame's command buffer invalidated. Root cause: TexturePool::release() stashed a handle to the free list without removing it from in_use, so the next recycle_frame() stashed the same handles a SECOND time; the free list accumulated duplicate handles and a frame acquired one texture for two live roles (attachment of one pass + sampled input of another in the same usage scope) — invalid command buffer, empty present, black preview. Same accounting bug existed in UniformBufferPool (latent). Fix: credit-count accounting — release() records a per-key credit, recycle_frame() skips that many in_use entries instead of re-stashing, so every handle enters the free list exactly once. Proof of test validity: the 3 new regression tests were run against the staged buggy texture_pool.rs and FAILED (recycle_never_duplicates_a_released_handle_in_the_free_list: duplicate handles detected; steady_state_frames_hand_out_only_distinct_textures: "scene and blend target must not alias, left: 13, right: 13" — the exact black-preview mechanism; a_released_and_reacquired_handle_is_returned_exactly_once: free list 2 vs 1), then PASS with the fix. Two pre-existing tests (free_list_saturates_at_the_cap, the_cap_is_applied_per_size_not_globally) and one uniform-pool test (retention_is_capped) were rewritten because their expectations were artifacts of the duplication bug (an immediate acquire-after-release loop re-pops the same handle, so under correct accounting the free list holds one entry, not 8 duplicate handles); they now hold targets live before releasing, which genuinely exercises the cap. cargo test -p compositor -p gpu -p effects -p masks = 31 pass / 0 fail (compositor 12, effects 12, gpu 7). wasm rebuilt (3,124,315 bytes, 17:03) and dev server restarted. Decisive browser verification, same probe same GPU same flow as the failing run: preview canvas 0 black / 4096 non-black pixels, ZERO validation errors (only Chrome's unrelated powerPreference notice), 0 createBuffer failures, element in timeline store. Full web suite unaffected: bun test --isolate src/ = 1111 pass / 0 fail / 11 skip.

t-5 GitHub security triage completed with every CI failure on main root-caused and fixed locally. (1) Dependency audit: bun audit on main reported 5 vulnerabilities incl. 2 CRITICAL RCE in next@16.2.11 (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4). Fixed by bumping next to 16.3.4 (root + apps/web) and pinning resolutions adm-zip 0.6.1 + baseline-browser-mapping 2.11.0; bun audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities across 833 packages. Post-bump validation: bun test --isolate src/ 1111 pass/0 fail, tsc --noEmit clean, dev server restarted on next 16.3.4 (log confirms "Next.js 16.3.4 (Turbopack)"), headed browser smoke (editor + import + drop photo + 6s render loop) = 0 console errors, 0 createBuffer failures. (2) Secret scan: reproduced the CI failure locally with official gitleaks 8.28.0 — 8 findings across 575 commits, all placeholders (your-*, build-time-secret, ci-only-secret-<hex>). Root cause of the false positives: the custom generic-api-key rule lacked secretGroup so gitleaks matched the key NAME against the allowlist regexes (which were written for values), making the allowlist dead code. Fixed .gitleaks.toml (secretGroup = 2, value-based allowlist regexes without quotes). Verification: full git history scan = 575 commits / 40.47 MB / 0 leaks / exit 0, while a scratch dir with a real-looking key still triggers detection (positive control). (3) Playwright CI failure (all 15 PRs "unstable"): root-caused via git history — apps/web dev script has hardcoded port 3005 since commit a36d16b but playwright.config.ts still polled 127.0.0.1:3000, so CI's webServer poll timed out and the whole suite failed on every PR. Fixed config to 3005 (+comment); installed missing chromium build; smoke spec = 3/3 passed locally. Full e2e suite was interrupted by the user and left for a manual run. (4) PR triage (15 Dependabot PRs, read-only via api.github.com): #93 serde 1.0.229, #94 uuid 1.26.0, #96/#97 tauri-plugin-fs/dialog patches, #99/#100 zod 4.5.4 = safe minor/patch bumps, CI green except the base-wide failures now fixed; #98/#101/#104/#105 next = redundant (manual 16.3.4 bump supersedes); #95 syn 3.0.4, #106/#107 motion 13.2.0, #108/#109 better-auth 1.7.3 = major bumps, not security-driven, deferred for dedicated validation. Recommended sequence (needs push rights, not executed per the no-destructive-action constraint): push local fixes first to green the base, then merge the patch/minor PRs, close the redundant next PRs, defer the majors.
